title: @param tag without a parameter variable name is malformed PHPDoc syntax

ground_truth.statement: Under the proposed PSR-5/PSR-19 PHPDoc tag specification, @param has the syntax '@param [<Type>] [...]$[name] [<description>]', requiring the parameter variable name prefixed with $. PHP itself ignores comments; countValidLabels() with @param string[] $labels is the valid control.

allowed.reason: Ignoring the malformed @param tag leaves a bare native array parameter without an element type. This is a correct secondary completeness diagnostic.

notes: Isolates a @param tag whose type (string[]) is valid but whose $variable name is omitted. PHPStan 2.3.1 reports phpDoc.parseError (plus secondary missingType.iterableValue), and Psalm 6.20.1 reports InvalidDocblock. Mago 1.60.2 (both analyze and lint --only valid-docblock) emits nothing and silently discards the @param tag, leaving $labels typed as array<array-key, mixed>.
